chunks: And it is narrated from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, who said:

I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a man who married a woman in mutʿah, then her family learned of it and married her to another man openly, while she was a truthful woman. He said: “She must not allow her husband access to herself until her waiting period and her stipulated term have ended.”

I said: “If her stipulated term is a year, and her husband cannot be patient for her?” He said: “Then her husband should have taqwa of Allah and cede to her whatever remains of his term. For indeed she has been afflicted, and the abode is an abode of truce, and the believers are in taqiyyah.”

I said: “If he cedes to her her remaining days and her waiting period ends, what should she do?” He said: “She should say to her husband when she enters upon him: ‘O man, my family rushed upon me and married me off without my command, and they did not seek my permission. But now I am pleased, so begin today and marry me in a valid marriage between me and you.’”

He said: And I said to al-Riḍā عليه السلام: “A woman marries in mutʿah, then her stipulated term ends, and she marries another man before her waiting period ends?” He said: “What is that upon you? The sin of that is only upon her.”

key_terms.إِثْمُ: sin and moral liability for the act
key_terms.تَزْوِيجًا صَحِيحًا: a valid and sound marriage contract
key_terms.تَقِيَّةٍ: religious precaution through concealment under difficult circumstances
key_terms.عِدَّتُهَا: her legally required waiting period before another marriage

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman in mutʿah is married off to another man before her term and ʿiddah have ended?
ai.summary: This hadith gives legal rulings concerning mutʿah, the waiting period, and a subsequent marriage arranged by the woman’s family without her authorization. It emphasizes that she may not permit marital relations until the prior term and ʿiddah are completed, and it also reflects the condition of taqiyyah and social difficulty faced by believers.
